cards.canonical_statement: For every natural n and real a, x ↦ x^n has derivative n*a^(n-1) at a; n-1 is truncated natural subtraction.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the natural-power derivative theorem, including n=0 without a nonzero-point premise.
sketch_steps: Fix an arbitrary natural exponent n and real evaluation point a.
Use the derivative theorem for the n-th natural power.
Interpret the coefficient as the natural-number cast into ℝ.
Interpret n-1 as Nat.pred n, so the formula also covers n=0.

cards.canonical_statement: For every natural n, the function x ↦ x^n is continuous on ℝ.
cards.proof_strategy: Apply closure of the continuous identity function under arbitrary natural powers.
sketch_steps: Fix an arbitrary natural exponent.
The real identity function is continuous.
Take its n-th power using continuity of multiplication.
Conclude global continuity, including the constant zeroth power.

cards.canonical_statement: For every natural n and real endpoints a,b, x^n is interval-integrable and its oriented integral equals (b^(n+1)-a^(n+1))/(n+1).
cards.proof_strategy: Combine continuity of natural powers with the power antiderivative formula.
sketch_steps: Fix n and arbitrary finite real endpoints.
Continuity gives interval integrability.
Use the antiderivative x^(n+1)/(n+1).
The denominator n+1 is positive, including when n=0.
Evaluate the antiderivative at b and a with the oriented convention.

cards.proof_strategy: Apply the natural-power chain rule at the actual image f(a).
sketch_steps: Fix f, its derivative u at a, and an arbitrary natural n.
Differentiate the outer natural-power map at f(a).
Compose with the derivative of f at a.
Multiply the outer slope by u; the formula includes n=0.

Apply substitution with the transformed endpoints f(a),f(b).
Preserve orientation, so no monotonicity hypothesis is introduced.

Apply interval-integral addition; no order on the endpoints is needed.
